Forbidden.description: Forbidden. Most often an ownership/authorization failure (Laravel's default `{"message": "..."}` shape). If the account is restricted by SendFox, the response instead carries the structured `account_restricted` body with a link to the account status page.

TooManyRequests.description: Rate limit reached: 60 requests per minute per user, shared across all endpoints. Wait for the `Retry-After` seconds, then try again.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests left in the current window.

error.example: API access is unavailable while the account is restricted.

AutomationEmailAction.description: Adds or removes a tag or list when a contact is sent, opens, or clicks an automation email.

ends_automation.description: Whether this also takes the contact out of the automation.

link_url.description: For a click action, the only link that runs it. Null means any link.

AutomationItem.description: A step in an automation: an email, or a condition that sends each contact down its Yes or No path. Steps on a path carry the condition's id in parent_item_id and the path in branch. send_order orders the steps within the flow they sit in (the main flow, or one path). Conditions are built in the SendFox app; the automation-emails endpoints only act on email steps.

actions.description: Returned by GET /automations/{id}. What runs when this email is sent, opened or clicked.

campaign_id.description: The step's email. Null for a condition.

condition_email_link_id.description: For clicked_previous, the link that must be clicked. Null means any link.

condition_type.description: What a condition checks. "Previous" is the nearest email before the condition.

delay_hours.description: Hours to wait before this step. For a condition, the wait before the contact is checked.

no_path_ends.description: Whether contacts leave the automation at the end of the No path, instead of continuing after the condition.

parent_item_id.description: The condition this step's path belongs to. Null for a step in the main flow.

yes_path_ends.description: Whether contacts leave the automation at the end of the Yes path, instead of continuing after the condition.

campaign_id.description: Set for open_campaign and click_campaign triggers; the campaign whose opens or clicks start the automation

contact_tag_id.description: Set for apply_tag triggers; the automation starts when a contact is given this tag

type.description: What starts the automation: a contact joining list_id (apply_list), being given contact_tag_id (apply_tag), opening campaign_id (open_campaign), or clicking a link in campaign_id (click_campaign). A contact is enrolled once per automation; a click also counts as an open.

filter.description: Human-readable rendering of the filter that was applied

matched_count.description: Number of contacts the filter matched; null until counted

is_web_gated.description: The saved per-issue signup requirement. Applies only to published web issues. If the account-wide signup requirement is enabled in Settings, the public page requires signup even when this field is false.

lists.description: The lists this campaign is addressed to, including any archived since, which `GET /lists` no longer returns. `GET /campaigns` returns only `id` and `name`, so compare against `GET /lists` to spot an archived one.

preview_text.description: Inbox preview snippet shown beneath the subject line in most email clients.

reply_to_email.description: Where replies go. Empty uses the account's default reply-to, then `from_email`.

link_stats.description: The campaign's links ranked by click count, most-clicked first. Present only when include_link_stats is true — it is the one part of this payload that queries rather than reading a stored counter.

bounce_paused_at.description: When this contact was last paused for repeated bounces. Can remain set after the pause has ended; read bounce_paused_until to tell.

bounce_paused_until.description: When the current repeated-bounce pause ends. Null if the contact isn't paused, or has since unsubscribed or become invalid, since no retry is coming.

bounced_at.description: When this address hard bounced. A hard bounce also sets unsubscribed_at. If unsubscribed_at is null, or far from this date, the bounce isn't what's stopping their email; they were resubscribed or opted out separately.

invalid_at.description: When this address was found to be invalid. It isn't mailed while this is set.

ContactFilter.description: An engagement filter over the account's contacts. Every condition is AND-ed. Omitting the object entirely means "all contacts".

clicked_campaign_id.description: Bulk actions only — not available on GET /contacts

in_list_ids.description: Contacts currently subscribed to at least one of these lists. Someone who unsubscribed from a list (via the unsubscribe page or the preference page) remains a member of it but is not matched here, so this filter can never reach people who opted out of the list it is built from. Changed with per-list unsubscribe: previously every member matched regardless of opt-out status, so results and counts may be smaller than before. Membership itself is unchanged and is still returned in full by GET /lists/{list_id}/contacts.

last_opened_before.description: Excludes contacts who never opened — use never_opened for those

not_in_list_ids.description: Contacts with no membership in any of these lists. Membership is what counts here, not subscription status, so someone who unsubscribed from a list is still excluded. A contact who opted out of list A therefore matches neither in_list_ids [A] nor not_in_list_ids [A].

not_opened_campaign_id.description: Contacts the campaign sent to who did not open it. Bulk actions only — not available on GET /contacts

not_tag_ids.description: Contacts carrying none of these tags. Carrying the tag is what counts here, not subscription status, so someone who opted out of a tag is still excluded. A contact who opted out of tag A therefore matches neither tag_ids [A] nor not_tag_ids [A].

opened_campaign_id.description: Bulk actions only — not available on GET /contacts

tag_ids.description: Contacts still subscribed to at least one of these tags. Someone who opted out of a tag (by keeping only some lists when they unsubscribed) keeps the tag but is not matched here, so this filter can never reach people who opted out of the tag it is built from. Changed with per-list unsubscribe, for the same reason and in the same way as in_list_ids: previously every tagged contact matched regardless of opt-out status, so results and counts may be smaller than before. The tag itself is unchanged and every carrier is still listed by the tag endpoints.

public_description.description: The name subscribers see for this list on the unsubscribe and preference pages, or null to show the list's own name.

subscribed_contacts_count.description: Members who can still be mailed from this list. Excludes anyone who unsubscribed from the list itself as well as anyone who unsubscribed from the account.

subscriber_description.description: What subscribers can expect from this list, shown below its name on the unsubscribe and preference pages. Returned by `GET /lists/{id}` and `PATCH /lists/{id}` only, not when lists are listed or embedded in a contact.

unsubscribed_contacts_count.description: Members who have stopped this list, by either the account-wide unsubscribe or this list's own. A hard bounce is included, because bouncing sets the account-wide flag. These two counts do not sum to total membership: an address flagged invalid is in neither.

list_unsubscribed_at.description: When this contact left this list, or null if they have not. They stay in `lists` either way, because leaving a list does not end membership. To know whether they can be mailed from a list, check that this is null AND the contact's own `unsubscribed_at` (the account-wide opt-out) and `invalid_at` are both null.

contacts_count.description: Number of contacts carrying the tag (included on list/show).

lists.description: The lists this contact belongs to, each with its own `list_unsubscribed_at`.

TransactionalBatchResult.description: One entry per item, in the order sent. An accepted item carries `id` and `status`; a refused one carries `error` in the catalog shape (without `request_id`, which is in the `x-request-id` header).

replayed.description: Present (`true`) when the item's `idempotency_key` matched an earlier email.

emails.description: 1 to 100 emails. Each item takes the same fields as `POST /transactional/emails` plus an optional `idempotency_key`. The `html` and `text` of all items together may total at most 5 MB.

idempotency_key.description: Optional, unique per logical email. Works like the `Idempotency-Key` header on the single route: within 24 hours the same key with the same item returns the original message (`replayed: true`); a different item is a per-item `invalid_idempotent_request` error.

TransactionalError.description: Every non-2xx response from a /transactional route.

fix.example: Verify the domain under Account > Domains, or send from the sandbox sender while testing.

message.example: The from address uses a domain this account has not verified.

name.description: Stable machine-readable error name (see the catalog in the Transactional section).

request_id.description: Also sent as the x-request-id header. Quote it to support.

reason.description: The receiving server's response, when there is one.

status.description: SMTP status code, when there is one (e.g. 5.1.1).

attachments.description: Only on `GET /transactional/emails/{id}`. The files sent with the email (never their content).

headers.description: The custom headers the email was sent with; `{}` when there were none.

id.description: Opaque message id (`tm_` and 24 hex characters). Store it as a string; it is random, not sequential.

mode.description: test for messages to the sandbox test addresses, which never reach a mailbox and are never counted.

attachments.description: Files to attach, at most 10 and 5 MB in total once decoded. Each is `{filename, content, content_type?}` with `content` the file in base64 (line breaks are fine). `content_type` is guessed from the extension when omitted and may carry parameters, like `text/calendar; method=REQUEST` for a calendar invite. Executable and script files (`.exe`, `.js`, `.bat`, `.scr`, ...) are refused, as are URLs (`path`): send the file itself. Not accepted on the batch endpoint. The file is kept only until the email is sent or fails; `GET /transactional/emails/{id}` shows its name, type and size.

bcc.description: At most 2 addresses; counts toward the 10-address total.

from.description: Sender. Either an address or a display name followed by one in angle brackets. The domain must be plain ASCII (for an internationalized domain, use its punycode form, starting xn--) and verified under Account > Domains (a subdomain of a verified domain also works), or be the sandbox sender `onboarding@sendfoxmail.com`, which needs no DNS but only delivers to your own account email and the test addresses (sandbox mail always shows the SendFox Onboarding display name).

headers.description: Custom headers, at most 20, as `{"Name": "value"}`. Allowed: `List-Unsubscribe`, `List-Unsubscribe-Post`, `List-Id`, `X-Entity-Ref-ID`, `References`, `In-Reply-To`, and any other `X-*` header except `X-SendFox-*` and `X-SG-*`. Headers SendFox or SendGrid set (`From`, `To`, `Cc`, `Bcc`, `Reply-To`, `Subject`, `Content-*`, `MIME-Version`, `Date`, `Message-ID`, `Return-Path`, `DKIM-Signature`, `Received`) are refused with a 422. Names may hold letters, digits and dashes; values may hold up to 998 characters and no line breaks. `List-Unsubscribe` must be one or more `mailto:` or `https:` URLs in angle brackets, and `List-Unsubscribe-Post` must be exactly `List-Unsubscribe=One-Click` with an `https:` URL in `List-Unsubscribe`, as RFC 8058 requires.

html.description: HTML body, at most 500 KB (UTF-8 bytes). Send html, text, or both.

tag.description: A label for grouping in the dashboard, for per-tag open/click tracking switches, and for per-tag alerts. Lowercase letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores. Messages without a tag are grouped by subject. Tags that look like authentication mail (`login_code`, `password_reset`, `otp`, ...) can never have tracking turned on. An account may hold at most 200 distinct tags, so tag by kind of email (`receipt`), not per customer or order.

text.description: Plain-text body, at most 100 KB (UTF-8 bytes). Send html, text, or both.

to.description: 1 to 10 addresses. to, cc and bcc together may hold at most 10, and every address counts as one email against your plan's sends, so a message to three people uses three.

dns.description: DNS records from SendGrid (included on show)

info.description:
# Introduction
SendFox's REST API lets you manage contacts, campaigns, lists, automations, and forms programmatically. It uses OAuth 2.0 for authentication.

Compatible with AI agents (Claude, ChatGPT, etc.) via the OpenAPI spec. Available at `GET /openapi.yaml`. There is also an MCP server at `https://sendfox.com/mcp`, which takes the same personal access token in the `Authorization` header, so no sign-in step is needed. Setup: https://sendfox.com/developer/mcp

# Authentication
### Personal Access Token
Create a personal access token at https://sendfox.com/account/oauth. Once created, use it in the `Authorization` header:
```
Authorization: Bearer {TOKEN}
```

### OAuth 2.0 Client
For integrations that require user authentication, create an OAuth 2.0 client at https://sendfox.com/account/oauth

* Authorization URL: https://sendfox.com/oauth/authorize
* Access Token URL: https://sendfox.com/oauth/token

# Personalization
Put these tags in an email's `subject` or `html`, on campaigns and automation emails. They are filled in for each contact when the email is sent.

| Tag | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `{{contact.first_name}}` | First name |
| `{{contact.last_name}}` | Last name |
| `{{contact.email}}` | Email address |
| `{{contact.fields.<name>}}` | A custom field, by the `name` from `GET /contact-fields` |
| `{{global.<name>}}` | An account-wide variable, managed in the app at https://sendfox.com/account/variables |

Add a fallback for empty values with a pipe: `{{contact.first_name | there}}`.

Campaign HTML sent through the API must include a `<body>` and an unsubscribe link using `{{unsubscribe_url}}` as its URL. Automation emails don't need the tag: SendFox adds the unsubscribe footer.

# Automation Sequences
A sequence is an automation with email steps:

1. `POST /automations` with a title and trigger: a list, a tag, or an open or click on an email.
2. `POST /automations/{id}/emails` for each step, with its `delay_hours`.
3. `POST /automation-emails/{id}/actions` to add or remove a tag or list when a step is sent, opened or clicked (optional).
4. `PATCH /automations/{id}` with `active: true`.

Branching conditions, A/B variants on a step, and adding existing contacts to an automation are done in the SendFox app.

# Rate Limits
API requests are limited to **60 requests per minute** per authenticated user. Rate limit status is returned in response headers:
- `X-RateLimit-Limit`: Maximum requests per minute
- `X-RateLimit-Remaining`: Remaining requests in current window
- `Retry-After`: Seconds until rate limit resets (only on 429 responses)

The limit is one shared budget per user across all endpoints, reads and writes alike, so a burst of writes also holds up your reads. Past it, requests return `429 Too Many Attempts.` until the window resets. Wait for the `Retry-After` seconds before retrying, and prefer `POST /contacts/batch` and `POST /contacts/bulk-actions` to one call per contact.

`/transactional/*` has its own burst and per-minute limits and doesn't count against this budget. `POST /campaigns/{id}/send-test` also has its own daily cap.

# Bounces and suppression
SendFox stops mailing addresses that can't receive email:
- **Hard bounce** (the receiving server says the mailbox doesn't exist): the contact is unsubscribed from the whole account and `bounced_at` is set. They get no more email unless they're resubscribed, either by you in the dashboard or by the person signing up on one of your forms again. They appear under `GET /contacts?filter[status]=bounced`, and not under `filter[status]=unsubscribed`, which is for people who opted out. `GET /contacts/unsubscribed` returns both.
- **Repeated bounces** (for example a mailbox that stays full): after 5 sends in a row bounce, over at least 14 days, the contact is paused for 30 days. `bounce_paused_at` says when it started and `bounce_paused_until` says when it ends (null once it has ended). The first email after that is a retry. If it's delivered, or the contact opens or clicks an email, the pause is over; if it bounces, they're paused again. A paused contact is still subscribed. They appear under `GET /contacts?filter[status]=bounce_paused`.
- **Other bounces** (for example a one-off rejection, or a problem on the sending side) are recorded on the send and don't change the contact.

# Error Responses
All error responses use standard HTTP status codes and Laravel's default error format:
- `message`: Human-readable error description
- `errors`: Field-level validation errors (on 422 responses)

# Plans & API Access
Every plan can create an API key. Lifetime and Pro plans get the whole API. The Free plan gets a limited set of endpoints: `GET /me`; reading lists, tags, contact tags, contact fields, campaigns and campaign stats, saved templates and sections, automations, and forms; creating contacts, adding a contact to a list, and tagging a contact; transactional email; and, on accounts with transactional access, sending domains. Any other endpoint returns `402 Payment Required` for a Free account. A key's access follows the account's plan, so upgrading opens the rest without a new key.

Accounts restricted by SendFox cannot use authenticated API endpoints. These requests return `403 Forbidden` with the error code `account_restricted` and a link to the account status page.

Queues one action against every contact the filter matches, applied in chunks in the
background. Returns immediately with an id to poll.

**Run with `dry_run: true` first.** A dry run reports how many contacts match and changes
nothing — it is the only way to catch a filter that matches more than intended, and a bulk
write is not undoable. An empty filter (which would match the whole account) is rejected
unless it is a dry run.

Per-campaign conditions (`opened_campaign_id`, `not_opened_campaign_id`,
`clicked_campaign_id`) are available here but not on `GET /contacts`, because they are
resolved in the background rather than inside a request.

Bulk delete and bulk unsubscribe are deliberately not offered.

Because `in_list_ids` matches only subscribed members, `remove_from_list` with
`filter.in_list_ids` set to that same list leaves the memberships of people who
unsubscribed from it in place. They already receive nothing from that list.

`tag_ids` behaves the same way, so `remove_tag` with `filter.tag_ids` set to that
same tag leaves the tag on people who unsubscribed from it. They already receive
nothing sent to that tag. To reach every carrier regardless of opt-out status,
select them by some other filter, or read them from the tag endpoints.

post.description:
Queues one email. The response is immediate; delivery happens in the
background and is reported through `GET /transactional/emails/{id}`
and your webhook.

**Idempotency.** Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (1 to 256 characters)
to make retries safe. Within 24 hours, the same key with the same body
returns the original message (with an `idempotent-replayed: true`
header); the same key with a different body is a `409
invalid_idempotent_request`.

**Sandbox.** Send from `onboarding@sendfoxmail.com` with no DNS setup.
It delivers only to your own account email and to the four test
addresses. Test addresses never reach a mailbox and never count toward
your limits; each one synthesizes an outcome so you can exercise your
integration: `delivered@sendfoxmail.com`, `bounced@sendfoxmail.com`,
`complained@sendfoxmail.com`, `suppressed@sendfoxmail.com`.

**Limits.** Transactional email has no quota of its own: every
address in `to`, `cc` and `bcc` counts as one send against your
SendFox plan, the same monthly sends your campaigns use, with no
daily cap. When the plan has a cap, every response carries
`x-sendfox-sends-remaining`, the sends left across campaigns and
transactional email; a plan without an enforced cap sends no header.
Past the cap, sends are refused with `429 monthly_quota_exceeded`
carrying `remaining` and `requested`. Each message holds at most 10
addresses across `to`, `cc` and `bcc`, at most 2 in `bcc`. Requests
are limited to 5 per second and 300 per minute per key.

**Custom headers.** Pass `headers` to add list-management and
threading headers. For one-click unsubscribe (RFC 8058, which Gmail
and Yahoo require of bulk senders) send `List-Unsubscribe` with an
`https:` URL in angle brackets and `List-Unsubscribe-Post` set to
`List-Unsubscribe=One-Click`; the URL must accept a `POST` whose body
is `List-Unsubscribe=One-Click` and unsubscribe the recipient without
any further click. See the `headers` field for what is allowed.

idempotent-replayed.description: Present (`true`) when an Idempotency-Key matched an earlier request.

x-sendfox-sends-remaining.description: Sends the plan has left, across campaigns and transactional email. Absent when the plan has no enforced cap.

403.description: insufficient_scope, domain_not_verified, sandbox_recipient_not_allowed, recipient_suppressed, account_paused, account_restricted

post.description:
Queues up to 100 emails in one request and reports a result per item.
Items are independent: one invalid address, unverified sender or
suppressed recipient is reported at its `index` and the rest are
queued. The response is `200` whenever the batch itself was accepted,
even if every item was refused; read each entry's `error`.

**Limits.** The whole batch's sends (one per `to`, `cc` and `bcc`
address across every item) are reserved against your plan before
any item is looked at. A batch that does not fit is refused with
`429 monthly_quota_exceeded` and nothing is sent, so a retry can
never half-send. Sends for refused items, test addresses and replays
are returned. A batch request counts as one request against the 5
per second and 300 per minute rate limit; the plan's sends are what
bound volume.

**Idempotency.** Two levels. An `Idempotency-Key` header makes the
whole batch replayable for 24 hours: the same key with the same
`emails` returns the original results with `idempotent-replayed: true`;
a different body is a `409 invalid_idempotent_request`. A per-item
`idempotency_key` protects each email on its own, exactly like the
header on `POST /transactional/emails`, and is the one to rely on when
your retry may be built from a different batch.

Sandbox, test addresses and tags work per item as on the single route.

to.0: The to.0 field must be a valid email address.

error.fix: See the errors object for each field.
error.message: The request body has invalid or missing fields.
error.name: validation_error

200.description: Batch accepted; one result per item

idempotent-replayed.description: Present (`true`) when an Idempotency-Key matched an earlier batch.

x-sendfox-sends-remaining.description: Sends the plan has left, across campaigns and transactional email. Absent when the plan has no enforced cap.

409.description: invalid_idempotent_request (the Idempotency-Key header was used with a different body)

422.description: validation_error on the envelope (`emails` missing, not a list, empty, over 100 items or over 5 MB)

429.description: rate_limit_exceeded, or monthly_quota_exceeded when the whole batch does not fit the plan's remaining sends

get.description: The message without its bodies, plus its event timeline.

tags.description:
Send email from your app, one per request or up to 100 per
batch: login codes, receipts, notifications. Unlike the rest of the API, transactional
routes are available on every plan, including free. Use any API key
from Settings > API tokens (the Transactional page makes your first one);
it works on every route your plan includes (see Plans & API Access), the
Domains endpoints included, so your app can add, verify and remove the
domains it sends from.
Transactional keys made before keys were unified carry `transactional:*`
scopes and keep working on these routes and `/domains` only; they are
rejected by the rest of the API.

Transactional is for messages your users trigger: password resets,
receipts, notifications about their own account. Newsletters,
promotions, re-engagement and review requests belong in SendFox
campaigns.

### Switching from Resend
Keep your code. Resend's SDKs read a base URL from the environment and
SendFox accepts Resend's request shape at `/transactional/resend`, so
the switch is two variables plus a verified domain:

```
RESEND_BASE_URL=https://api.sendfox.com/transactional/resend
RESEND_API_KEY=<your SendFox transactional key>
```

`resend.emails.send()`, `resend.batch.send()` and `resend.emails.get()`
then go to `POST /transactional/resend/emails`,
`POST /transactional/resend/emails/batch` and
`GET /transactional/resend/emails/{id}`: `to`, `cc` and `bcc` may be a
string or an array, `reply_to` may be a one-item array, and
`tags: [{name, value}]` becomes the SendFox `tag` (the first value).
Every recipient counts as one send against your plan, as Resend counts
them, and a message may carry up to 10 addresses (Resend allows 50). Responses and errors are SendFox's
(`202 {id, status}`, and the error catalog below with `name`, `message`
and `fix`). `attachments` work as on Resend (`{filename, content,
content_type}`, with content in base64 or a byte array), except `path`
URLs and inline images (`content_id`), which are refused.
`scheduled_at` is not supported yet. Anything unsupported is refused
with a `422 validation_error` rather than sent without it. For webhooks, set your endpoint to the Resend format (see
Webhooks below) and your existing handler and signature check keep
working with the SendFox secret.

### Error catalog
Every non-2xx response has the same shape: `status`, `name`,
`message`, `fix`, `link`, `request_id`.

| Status | name | When |
|---|---|---|
| 401 | `missing_api_key` | No Authorization header |
| 401 | `invalid_api_key` | The key is wrong or revoked |
| 403 | `insufficient_scope` | A free-plan key without the needed transactional scope |
| 403 | `domain_not_verified` | The from domain is not verified for this account |
| 403 | `sandbox_recipient_not_allowed` | Sandbox sender to an address that is not yours |
| 403 | `recipient_suppressed` | A recipient is on your suppression list (`suppressed` lists them) |
| 403 | `account_paused` | Transactional sending is paused for review |
| 403 | `account_restricted` | The SendFox account is restricted |
| 404 | `not_found` | No message with that id on this account |
| 409 | `invalid_idempotent_request` | Same Idempotency-Key, different body, inside 24 hours |
| 422 | `validation_error` | Field errors in `errors` |
| 429 | `rate_limit_exceeded` | Over 5/s or 300/min; honor `Retry-After` |
| 429 | `monthly_quota_exceeded` | The plan's sends are used up (`remaining`, `requested`); upgrade the SendFox plan from Account > Billing |

### Webhooks
Add one https URL under Transactional > Webhooks and SendFox POSTs a
JSON event to it for each of `sent`, `delivered`, `delayed`, `bounced`,
`complained` and `failed` that you pick. Sandbox test addresses send
events too. The URL must resolve to a public address; redirects are not
followed, and SendFox waits up to 10 seconds for an answer.

```json
{
  "id": "whd_5f0c2a9e1b7d4c3a8e6f1d2b",
  "event": "delivered",
  "occurred_at": "2026-10-10T14:03:22+00:00",
  "data": {
    "message": { "id": "tm_…", "status": "delivered", "to": ["ada@example.com"], "subject": "Your code", "tag": "login_code", "…": "same fields as GET /transactional/emails/{id}, without events" },
    "recipient": "ada@example.com",
    "status": null,
    "reason": null
  }
}
```

`recipient` is the address the event is about (a message with `cc`
gets one event per recipient). `status` and `reason` carry the
receiving server's answer on `bounced`, `delayed` and `failed`.

Any 2xx answer counts as delivered. Anything else, or no answer, is
retried after 1 minute, 15 minutes, 2 hours and 18 hours, then given
up. Retries send the same body with the same `id`, so dedupe on it.

**Verify every request.** The `X-SendFox-Signature` header is
`t={unix seconds},v1={hex}`, where `hex` is HMAC-SHA256 of
`{t}.{raw body}` keyed with your signing secret (the whole `whsec_…`
string). Compute it over the raw body before parsing the JSON, compare
in constant time, and reject a `t` more than five minutes old. Requests
also carry `X-SendFox-Event` and `X-SendFox-Delivery` (the body's `id`).

**Resend format.** Switching from Resend? Set the webhook's format to
Resend under Transactional > Webhooks and the body is shaped like a
Resend event instead, with the same event types (`email.sent`,
`email.delivered`, `email.delivery_delayed`, `email.bounced`,
`email.complained`, `email.failed`) and `svix-id`, `svix-timestamp`
and `svix-signature` headers signed the way Svix signs, so your
existing handler and `webhooks.verify()` call keep working with the
SendFox secret. `data.email_id` is the SendFox `tm_` id, `data.tags`
is `{"tag": "<your tag>"}`, a bounce or delay carries Resend's
`bounce` object with the receiving server's reason, and
`data.recipient` names the address the event is about.

```json
{
  "type": "email.bounced",
  "created_at": "2026-10-10T14:03:22+00:00",
  "data": {
    "created_at": "2026-10-10T14:03:20+00:00",
    "email_id": "tm_…",
    "from": "Acme <hello@mail.acme.com>",
    "to": ["ada@example.com"],
    "subject": "Your code",
    "tags": { "tag": "login_code" },
    "bounce": { "message": "550 5.1.1 User unknown", "subType": "5.1.1", "type": "Permanent" },
    "recipient": "ada@example.com"
  }
}
```
